        valuation_offset_account_id=event.wip_account_id,
    )
    await docflow.link_documents(
        session,
        event.tenant_id,
        predecessor=event.document_id,
        successor=move.document_id,
        link_type=PRODUCTION_ORDER_FINISHED_TO_MOVE_LINK,
    )


async def disposition_rejected_stock(
    session: AsyncSession, event: InspectionDispositioned
) -> None:
    """Move the REJECTED stock for a rejected inspection lot (D-050), in the decision's transaction
    —
    the quality twin of the GR/delivery bridges.

    SCRAP → an ADJUSTMENT-out (``from_bin`` set, no ``to_bin``): the costing engine offsets an
    ADJUSTMENT-down to the price-difference / inventory-adjustment account (the write-off), so the
    move posts Dr inventory-adjustment / Cr Inventory at the stock's book value — total on-hand
    drops. BLOCK → a TRANSFER from the receiving bin to the event's blocked/QI bin: value-neutral (a
    within-warehouse transfer publishes no costing journal), so total on-hand is unchanged but the
    stock leaves the usable bin. The costing engine COMPUTES the cost of the stock that left, so no
    unit_cost is passed. Insufficient stock at the bin raises InsufficientStockError, rolling the
    decision back (D-020). Links the inspection-lot document → 'dispositioned_by' → move document.
    Registered via ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (not an import-time ``@on``)."""
    move_date = date.fromisoformat(event.move_date)
    disposition = RejectDisposition(event.disposition)
    if disposition == RejectDisposition.SCRAP:
        payload = StockMoveCreate(
            move_type=MoveType.ADJUSTMENT,
            item_id=event.item_id,
            quantity=event.rejected_quantity,
            from_bin_id=event.from_bin_id,
            lot_id=event.inventory_lot_id,
            serial_id=event.serial_id,
            move_date=move_date,
            reference=event.lot_number,
        )
    else:  # BLOCK — a quarantine transfer to the blocked bin
        payload = StockMoveCreate(
            move_type=MoveType.TRANSFER,
            item_id=event.item_id,
            quantity=event.rejected_quantity,
            from_bin_id=event.from_bin_id,
            to_bin_id=event.to_bin_id,
            lot_id=event.inventory_lot_id,
            serial_id=event.serial_id,
            move_date=move_date,
            reference=event.lot_number,
        )
    move = await create_move(session, event.tenant_id, payload)
    await docflow.link_documents(
        session,
        event.tenant_id,
        predecessor=event.document_id,
        successor=move.document_id,
        link_type=INSPECTION_DISPOSITIONED_BY_MOVE_LINK,
    )


async def provision_inventory_for_template(
    session: AsyncSession, event: IndustryTemplateApplying
) -> None:
    """Create the inventory slice (UoMs + item categories) of an applied industry template (PLAN
    14.1, D-060), idempotently, in the apply's transaction — the §5-clean provisioning seam: the
    industry module publishes ``IndustryTemplateApplying`` and inventory reacts here, creating ITS
    OWN master rows through its own models (industry never imports inventory/service).

    Idempotency (D-060): every create is SKIP-IF-EXISTS by code (the natural key), so re-applying
    the same template never duplicates. Item categories carry the template's default costing method
    (retail/healthcare FIFO, manufacturing/construction moving-average) but NO GL-account wiring —
    that is wired later when stocked items post moves (D-029); a provisioning preset only seeds the
    method. Runs under ``system_context`` so tenant_id is stamped explicitly. Registered via
    ``app.main.register_event_handlers`` (the D-011 seam)."""
    template = event.template
    tenant_id = event.tenant_id
    with system_context():
        existing_uoms = {
            code
            for (code,) in (
                await session.execute(select(Uom.code).where(Uom.tenant_id == tenant_id))
            ).all()
        }
        for uom in template.uoms:
            if uom.code not in existing_uoms:
                session.add(Uom(tenant_id=tenant_id, code=uom.code, name=uom.name))
        existing_categories = {
            code
            for (code,) in (
                await session.execute(
                    select(ItemCategory.code).where(ItemCategory.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                )
            ).all()
        }
        for category in template.item_categories:
            if category.code in existing_categories:
                continue
            session.add(
                ItemCategory(
                    tenant_id=tenant_id,
                    code=category.code,
                    name=category.name,
                    default_costing_method=CostingMethod(
                        category.default_costing_method
                    ).value,
                )
            )
        await session.flush()


__all__ = [
    "disposition_rejected_stock",
    "issue_delivery_moves",
    "issue_production_components",
    "provision_inventory_for_template",
    "receive_finished_order_move",
    "receive_goods_receipt_moves",
    "receive_return_moves",
]

# Inventory Module Research Report

## 1. Router files — module is split into FOUR router files, one mount point

`backend/app/modules/inventory/router.py` is the top-level router (`prefix="/api/v1/inventory"`). It owns item-categories/uoms/items/uom-conversions (PLAN 5.1) and mounts three sibling sub-routers at the bottom via `router.include_router(...)` (same precedent as finance's journal_router/ap_router — one HTTP surface, multiple files):

- `stock_router.py` — warehouses, bins, stock-moves, on-hand projection (PLAN 5.2)
- `valuation_router.py` — stock-valuations, cost-layers (PLAN 5.3)
- `count_router.py` — physical/cycle counts (PLAN 5.4)

Schemas are split too: `schemas.py` (5.1/5.2/5.3 types) and `count_schemas.py` (5.4 types, split at the 400-line cap).

All endpoints require `CurrentUserDep`/`SessionDep`; writes run inside `run_in_uow` (D-011); GETs on reference data (categories, uoms, warehouses, bins) support conditional GET via collection ETag; transactional/fast-changing lists (items*, moves, on-hand, valuations, cost-layers, counts, count-lines) carry no ETag. (*items get an ETag too, folded with filters into the fingerprint — see code.)

---

## 2. Full endpoint list, grouped by concept

All paths are relative to `/api/v1/inventory`.

### Item categories
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/item-categories` | `inventory.category.read` | — | `Page[ItemCategoryRead]` | yes (cursor) | no |
| POST | `/item-categories` | `inventory.category.manage` | `ItemCategoryCreate` | `ItemCategoryRead` (201) | single | no |
| GET | `/item-categories/{category_id}` | `inventory.category.read` | — | `ItemCategoryRead` | single | no |
| PATCH | `/item-categories/{category_id}` | `inventory.category.manage` | `ItemCategoryUpdate` | `ItemCategoryRead` | single | no |

### Units of measure
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/uoms` | `inventory.uom.read` | — | `Page[UomRead]` | yes | no |
| POST | `/uoms` | `inventory.uom.manage` | `UomCreate` | `UomRead` (201) | single | no |
| GET | `/uoms/{uom_id}` | `inventory.uom.read` | — | `UomRead` | single | no |
| PATCH | `/uoms/{uom_id}` | `inventory.uom.manage` | `UomUpdate` | `UomRead` | single | no |

### Items
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/items?item_type&category_id&is_active` | `inventory.item.read` | — | `Page[ItemRead]` | yes | no |
| POST | `/items` | `inventory.item.manage` | `ItemCreate` | `ItemRead` (201) | single | no |
| GET | `/items/{item_id}` | `inventory.item.read` | — | `ItemRead` | single | no |
| PATCH | `/items/{item_id}` | `inventory.item.manage` | `ItemUpdate` | `ItemRead` | single | no |
| GET | `/items/{item_id}/uom-conversions` | `inventory.item.read` | — | `list[UomConversionRead]` | no (plain list) | no |
| POST | `/items/{item_id}/uom-conversions` | `inventory.item.manage` | `UomConversionCreate` | `UomConversionRead` (201) | single | no |

None of the masters (category/uom/item/conversion writes) are idempotency-keyed — they're not "documents" in the D-012/D-013 sense, just reference-data CRUD.

### Warehouses
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/warehouses` | `inventory.warehouse.read` | — | `Page[WarehouseRead]` | yes | no |
| POST | `/warehouses` | `inventory.warehouse.manage` | `WarehouseCreate` | `WarehouseRead` (201) | single | no |
| GET | `/warehouses/{warehouse_id}` | `inventory.warehouse.read` | — | `WarehouseRead` | single | no |
| PATCH | `/warehouses/{warehouse_id}` | `inventory.warehouse.manage` | `WarehouseUpdate` | `WarehouseRead` | single | no |

### Bins
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/bins?warehouse_id` | `inventory.bin.read` | — | `Page[BinRead]` | yes | no |
| POST | `/bins` | `inventory.bin.manage` | `BinCreate` | `BinRead` (201) | single | no |
| GET | `/bins/{bin_id}` | `inventory.bin.read` | — | `BinRead` | single | no |
| PATCH | `/bins/{bin_id}` | `inventory.bin.manage` | `BinUpdate` | `BinRead` | single | no |

### Stock moves (the ledger)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/stock-moves` | `inventory.move.create` | `StockMoveCreate` | `StockMoveRead` (201) | single | **YES** — `Idempotent("inventory.stock_move.create")` |
| POST | `/stock-moves/{move_id}/reverse` | `inventory.move.create` | — | `StockMoveRead` (201, the NEW reversing move) | single | **YES** — `Idempotent("inventory.stock_move.reverse")` |
| GET | `/stock-moves?item_id&bin_id&move_type&date_from&date_to` | `inventory.move.read` | — | `Page[StockMoveRead]` | yes | no |
| GET | `/stock-moves/{move_id}` | `inventory.move.read` | — | `StockMoveRead` | single | no |

There is **no PATCH/DELETE** on a move — it's posted-at-creation and immutable; corrections are only via `/reverse`.

### On-hand projection
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/stock-on-hand?item_id&bin_id` | `inventory.move.read` | — | `Page[StockOnHandRead]` | yes | no |

Note: on-hand read uses the SAME permission as move read (`inventory.move.read`), not a separate key.

### Valuation
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/stock-valuations?item_id&warehouse_id` | `inventory.valuation.read` | — | `Page[StockValuationRead]` | yes | no |
| GET | `/items/{item_id}/cost-layers?warehouse_id&include_exhausted` | `inventory.valuation.read` | — | `Page[CostLayerRead]` | yes | no |

### Stock counts (physical/cycle)
| Method | Path | Permission | Body | Response | Paginated | Idem-Key |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/stock-counts` | `inventory.count.manage` | `StockCountCreate` | `StockCountRead` (201) | single | **YES** — `Idempotent("inventory.stock_count.create")` |
| GET | `/stock-counts?status&warehouse_id&count_type` | `inventory.count.read` | — | `Page[StockCountRead]` | yes | no |
| GET | `/stock-counts/{count_id}` | `inventory.count.read` | — | `StockCountRead` | single | no |
| GET | `/stock-counts/{count_id}/lines` | `inventory.count.read` | — | `Page[StockCountLineRead]` | yes | no |
| GET | `/stock-counts/{count_id}/variance-preview` (cursor params too) | `inventory.count.read` | — | `StockCountVariancePreview` (contains its own `Page[StockCountVarianceLine]` inside `lines`) | mixed — outer object, inner `lines` paginated | no |
| POST | `/stock-counts/{count_id}/lines/{line_id}/count` | `inventory.count.manage` | `StockCountLineCountUpdate` | `StockCountLineRead` | single | no (last-write-wins field update, not document-creating) |
| POST | `/stock-counts/{count_id}/post` | `inventory.count.post` | — | `StockCountRead` **OR** `JobSubmitted` (202) | single | **YES** — `Idempotent("inventory.stock_count.post")` |
| POST | `/stock-counts/{count_id}/cancel` | `inventory.count.manage` | — | `StockCountRead` | single | no |

**Important frontend implication for `/post`:** response is a discriminated union. If the count has ≤ `COUNT_POST_SYNC_MAX_VARIANCES` (200) non-zero-variance lines (estimated from the snapshot), it posts inline and returns `StockCountRead` with `status=200`. Above that, it returns `202 {job_id, status}` (`JobSubmitted`) and the frontend must poll `/api/v1/jobs/{job_id}` (the same pattern as finance's bank-import/depreciation-run). You'll need to inspect `response.status_code` (200 vs 202) or check for the `job_id` field to discriminate client-side.

---

## 3. Permission constants (`inventory/constants.py`)

```
INVENTORY_ITEM_READ        = "inventory.item.read"        # Read items and their UoM conversions
INVENTORY_ITEM_MANAGE       = "inventory.item.manage"       # Create/edit items and UoM conversions
INVENTORY_CATEGORY_READ    = "inventory.category.read"     # Read item categories
INVENTORY_CATEGORY_MANAGE  = "inventory.category.manage"   # Create/edit item categories
INVENTORY_UOM_READ         = "inventory.uom.read"           # Read units of measure
INVENTORY_UOM_MANAGE       = "inventory.uom.manage"         # Create/edit units of measure
INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_READ   = "inventory.warehouse.read"     # Read warehouses
INVENTORY_WAREHOUSE_MANAGE = "inventory.warehouse.manage"   # Create/edit warehouses
INVENTORY_BIN_READ         = "inventory.bin.read"           # Read storage bins
INVENTORY_BIN_MANAGE       = "inventory.bin.manage"         # Create/edit storage bins
INVENTORY_MOVE_READ        = "inventory.move.read"          # Read move ledger + on-hand
INVENTORY_MOVE_CREATE      = "inventory.move.create"        # Create moves (receipt/issue/transfer/adjustment)
INVENTORY_VALUATION_READ   = "inventory.valuation.read"     # Read valuations + FIFO cost layers
INVENTORY_COUNT_READ       = "inventory.count.read"         # Read counts and variances
INVENTORY_COUNT_MANAGE     = "inventory.count.manage"       # Create counts, record counted qty, cancel
INVENTORY_COUNT_POST       = "inventory.count.post"         # Post count variances as adjustment moves (privileged)
```

No separate "delete" permission anywhere — nothing in this module is deletable (soft-deactivate via `is_active` on warehouses/bins/items; moves/counts are append-only).

---

## 4. Full schema definitions

All from `ApiModel` (Pydantic v2, `use_enum_values=True` → enums serialize as their UPPER_SNAKE string). Decimals serialize as strings (D-015) — type them as `string` in TS and format via lib/format.ts, mirroring finance.

### Item categories
```
ItemCategoryCreate: { code: str, name: str, default_costing_method: CostingMethod = MOVING_AVERAGE,
  inventory_account_id: UUID|null, cogs_account_id: UUID|null, price_difference_account_id: UUID|null }
ItemCategoryUpdate: { name?, default_costing_method?, inventory_account_id?, cogs_account_id?, price_difference_account_id? }  (code immutable)
ItemCategoryRead: { id, code, name, default_costing_method, inventory_account_id: UUID|null,
  cogs_account_id: UUID|null, price_difference_account_id: UUID|null, created_at, updated_at }
```
The three account ids are opaque finance GL-account UUIDs (D-029, no cross-module FK) — nullable; required (validated server-side) before a STOCKED item's category can post moves.

### UoM
```
UomCreate: { code: str, name: str }
UomUpdate: { name?: str }   (code immutable)
UomRead:   { id, code, name, created_at, updated_at }
```

### Items
```
ItemCreate: {
  item_code: str, name: str, description?: str,
  item_type: ItemType,                 # STOCKED | NON_STOCKED | SERVICE
  category_id: UUID, base_uom_id: UUID,
  costing_method?: CostingMethod,      # optional — defaults from category if omitted
  tracking_mode: TrackingMode = NONE,  # NONE | LOT | SERIAL
  is_active: bool = true,
  reorder_point?: Decimal, reorder_quantity?: Decimal
}
ItemUpdate: { name?, description?, category_id?, base_uom_id?, costing_method?, tracking_mode?,
  is_active?, reorder_point?, reorder_quantity? }   (item_code, item_type immutable)
ItemRead: { id, item_code, name, description: str|null, item_type, category_id, base_uom_id,
  costing_method, tracking_mode, is_active, reorder_point: Decimal|null, reorder_quantity: Decimal|null,
  created_at, updated_at }
ItemFilter (query params, not body): { item_type?, category_id?, is_active? }
```

### UoM conversions (nested under item)
```
UomConversionCreate: { alt_uom_id: UUID, factor_to_base: Decimal }   # item_id from path
UomConversionRead: { id, item_id, alt_uom_id, factor_to_base: Decimal, created_at }
```
`factor_to_base`: multiply an alt-UoM qty by this to get base-UoM qty (base EA, alt BOX, factor 12 ⇒ 1 BOX = 12 EA). DB CHECK `> 0`.

### Warehouses / bins
```
WarehouseCreate: { code: str, name: str, is_active: bool = true }
WarehouseUpdate: { name?, is_active? }   (code immutable)
WarehouseRead: { id, code, name, is_active, created_at, updated_at }

BinCreate: { warehouse_id: UUID, code: str, name: str, is_default: bool = false, is_active: bool = true }
BinUpdate: { name?, is_default?, is_active? }   (code, warehouse_id immutable)
BinRead: { id, warehouse_id, code, name, is_default, is_active, created_at, updated_at }
```
`is_default` marks the warehouse's default receiving bin — "exactly one default per warehouse" is a service convention, NOT a DB constraint (no partial unique index yet — so a naive frontend that assumes uniqueness could be surprised; don't over-trust it without checking).

### Stock moves
```
StockMoveCreate: {
  move_type: MoveType,              # RECEIPT | ISSUE | TRANSFER | ADJUSTMENT
  item_id: UUID, quantity: Decimal, # ALWAYS positive, in item's base UoM
  from_bin_id?: UUID, to_bin_id?: UUID,
  lot_id?: UUID, serial_id?: UUID,
  lot_code?: str, serial_code?: str,   # RECEIPT only: creates a NEW lot/serial master on the fly
  move_date?: date,                    # defaults to today
  reference?: str,
  unit_cost?: Decimal                  # REQUIRED on RECEIPT / positive ADJUSTMENT; ignored otherwise
}
StockMoveRead: {
  id, move_number: str,             # gapless "STK-2026-00001"
  move_type, item_id, quantity: Decimal, base_uom_id: UUID,
  from_bin_id: UUID|null, to_bin_id: UUID|null,
  lot_id: UUID|null, serial_id: UUID|null,
  move_date: date, reference: str|null, posted: bool,
  unit_cost: Decimal|null,           # entry cost (receipt) or engine-computed cost (issue)
  document_id: UUID, created_at
}
StockMoveFilter (query params): { item_id?, bin_id?, move_type?, date_from?: date, date_to?: date }
```
Bin-side rules per `move_type` (enforced server-side, mirror in your form validation):
- RECEIPT: `to_bin_id` required, `from_bin_id` must be null
- ISSUE: `from_bin_id` required, `to_bin_id` must be null
- TRANSFER: both required and must differ
- ADJUSTMENT: exactly one of the two set (populated side carries the signed intent — `to_bin_id` = increase, `from_bin_id` = decrease)

### On-hand
```
StockOnHandRead: { item_id: UUID, bin_id: UUID, lot_id: UUID|null, on_hand_qty: Decimal }
```
This is a maintained-projection quant row (`inv_stock_quants`), not a computed SUM — an indexed point read.

### Valuation
```
StockValuationRead: { item_id, warehouse_id, on_hand_qty: Decimal, avg_unit_cost: Decimal, total_value: Decimal }
CostLayerRead: { id, item_id, warehouse_id, receipt_move_id, received_at: date,
  original_qty: Decimal, remaining_qty: Decimal, unit_cost: Decimal, created_at }
```
`StockValuationRead` is only meaningful for `MOVING_AVERAGE` items; `CostLayerRead` (paginated oldest-first) only for `FIFO` items.

### Stock counts (`count_schemas.py`)
```
StockCountCreate: {
  count_type: CountType,       # PHYSICAL | CYCLE
  warehouse_id: UUID,
  count_date?: date, description?: str,
  item_ids?: UUID[], bin_ids?: UUID[]   # CYCLE only — ignored on PHYSICAL
}
StockCountLineCountUpdate: { counted_qty: Decimal }   # must be >= 0

StockCountRead: { id, count_number: str,   # gapless "CNT-2026-00001"
  count_type, warehouse_id, status: CountStatus,   # DRAFT|COUNTING|POSTED|CANCELLED
  count_date: date, description: str|null, posted_at: datetime|null,
  document_id, created_at, updated_at }

StockCountLineRead: { id, count_id, line_number: int, item_id, bin_id, lot_id: UUID|null,
  system_qty: Decimal, counted_qty: Decimal|null, variance_qty: Decimal|null,
  adjustment_move_id: UUID|null, unit_cost: Decimal|null }

StockCountVarianceLine: { line_id, item_id, bin_id, lot_id: UUID|null,
  system_qty: Decimal, counted_qty: Decimal|null, variance_qty: Decimal|null,
  unit_cost: Decimal, estimated_value_impact: Decimal }

StockCountVariancePreview: { count_id, status: CountStatus, lines: Page[StockCountVarianceLine],
  total_value_impact: Decimal }

StockCountFilter (query params): { status?, warehouse_id?, count_type? }
```
`system_qty` on `StockCountLineRead` is the SNAPSHOT at creation/last-recount, not necessarily live — the variance-preview endpoint re-reads live on-hand for its own `system_qty` field (which can differ from the line's stale value if stock moved between snapshot and preview).

### Shared: `JobSubmitted` (core/schemas.py, used by count-post 202) and `Page[T]`
```
JobSubmitted: { job_id: UUID, status: str }
Page<T>: { items: T[], next_cursor: string|null, limit: number }
```

---

## 5. Core concepts and relationships

**Item** (master, `inv_items`) — the terminology-locked "item" (never product/sku). Fields: `item_code` (user-supplied, unique per tenant, immutable), `name`, `description`, `item_type` (`ItemType`: STOCKED/NON_STOCKED/SERVICE — decides stock participation), `category_id` → `ItemCategory`, `base_uom_id` → `Uom` (the unit everything is stored/costed in), `costing_method` (`CostingMethod`: MOVING_AVERAGE/FIFO — defaulted from category at create, then stored on item, changeable only while zero stock), `tracking_mode` (`TrackingMode`: NONE/LOT/SERIAL — only valid on STOCKED items), `is_active`, `reorder_point`/`reorder_quantity` (planning fields, reorder logic lands in procurement 6.4).

**ItemCategory** — groups items by default costing method + the three finance GL account ids (`inventory_account_id`, `cogs_account_id`, `price_difference_account_id`) that costing needs. A STOCKED item's category must have all three wired or its moves 422 with `inventory.category_accounts_unwired`.

**Uom / UomConversion** — a UOM is just an identity (EA, KG, BOX); "base-ness" is per-item. `UomConversion.factor_to_base` expresses 1 alt-unit = factor × base-unit.

**Warehouse / Bin** — Warehouse groups Bins; on-hand is tracked PER BIN (`inv_stock_quants` keyed by item+bin+lot). Both reference data, soft-deactivated via `is_active` (never deleted since moves/quants reference them).

**StockMove** (`inv_stock_moves`) — the quantity SSOT, one append-only row per movement. **Immutable, POSTED at creation, no draft state** (the `MoveStatus` enum only ever holds `POSTED` — reserved for a future draft lifecycle but unused today). `quantity` is always positive; `move_type` (`MoveType`: RECEIPT/ISSUE/TRANSFER/ADJUSTMENT) decides which of `from_bin_id`/`to_bin_id` are populated, so direction is structural not signed. Carries a gapless `move_number` ("STK-2026-00001", claimed at creation via `DocumentMixin`). Reversal is a NEW opposite move via `/reverse`, linked via docflow `'reverses'`; a move can be reversed only once (second attempt → 409 `inventory.move_already_reversed`).

**StockQuant** (`inv_stock_quants`, NOT directly exposed — surfaced via the `/stock-on-hand` endpoint as `StockOnHandRead`) — the MAINTAINED PROJECTION of on-hand per (item, bin, lot), updated in the same transaction as every move. **This is the answer to your "stored vs projected" question: it is a stored, maintained balance, updated transactionally alongside the move — NOT a live SUM over history** (same architectural pattern as finance's projections, though the move ledger itself IS the append-only SSOT, mirroring the Universal Journal philosophy). DB `CHECK(on_hand_qty >= 0)` plus a pre-flight service check (`InsufficientStockError`) forbid negative stock on both engines. A quant row that reaches exactly 0 is deleted (so `on_hand_by_bin` never lists empty bins).

**Valuation** — `ItemValuation` (moving-average state per item+warehouse: on_hand, avg_unit_cost, total_value) and `CostLayer`/`LayerConsumption` (FIFO layers, oldest-first consumption, exact-reversal via replaying `LayerConsumption` rows backward). **Both are exposed read-only** via `/stock-valuations` and `/items/{id}/cost-layers`. Valuation is per (item, **warehouse**), not per bin — transfers within one warehouse are value-neutral (no journal); cross-warehouse transfers move value with the stock but net to zero GL effect (single inventory account in v1).

**StockCount** (`inv_stock_counts`) — a count document (gapless `count_number`, "CNT-2026-00001"). `count_type`: PHYSICAL (whole-warehouse snapshot) vs CYCLE (chosen `item_ids`/`bin_ids`). `status` lifecycle: `DRAFT` → `COUNTING` (first counted qty recorded) → `POSTED` (terminal) | `CANCELLED` (only from DRAFT/COUNTING). **StockCountLine** — one row per (item, bin, lot) in scope, snapshotting `system_qty` at creation; `counted_qty` recorded via the line-count endpoint; `variance_qty`/`adjustment_move_id`/`unit_cost` filled only at post.

### How variances reconcile to finance (the key semantic you asked about)
Counting does **not** post a bespoke journal entry. Posting a count re-reads **live** on-hand per line (not the stale snapshot — protects against stock moving between snapshot and post) and, for every non-zero variance, posts **one ordinary ADJUSTMENT stock move** via the same `stock_moves.create_move` engine every other move uses. That move runs through the normal costing engine (`apply_costing`) which publishes a `StockValued` domain event; `finance/handlers.py` subscribes to that event and posts the GL journal (Dr/Cr inventory vs price-difference account) — **all in the same transaction** as the count post. So: count → adjustment move → StockValued event → finance journal, one atomic unit of work. A positive variance enters stock at the item's *current book cost* (`queries.current_unit_cost`, not an arbitrary price); a negative variance is costed by the engine (moving-average/FIFO) like any issue. Zero-variance lines generate no move and no journal (`adjustment_move_id` stays null).

### What happens when you try to move more stock than is on hand
`apply_bin_delta` in `service/stock_quants.py` pre-flight-checks the decrement before writing; if it would go negative it raises `InsufficientStockError` (`ValidationFailedError` subclass, HTTP 422, code `inventory.insufficient_stock`, details `{item_id, bin_id, requested, available}`). The DB `CHECK(on_hand_qty >= 0)` is the backstop if that check is ever bypassed. Applies to ISSUE, TRANSFER (from-side), ADJUSTMENT-down, and to a reversal that would itself go negative.

### Are moves reversible?
Yes, via `POST /stock-moves/{move_id}/reverse` — creates a NEW move with bins swapped (RECEIPT↔ISSUE retype; TRANSFER/ADJUSTMENT keep their type but the populated side flips), linked via docflow `'reverses'`. The reversal replays the original's FIFO consumptions backward / re-adds moving-average value and publishes the opposite `StockValued` event so the GL journal is reversed too. A move can only be reversed once.

### Cross-module event bridges you should know about (backend-only, informs what shows up in the ledger, not new UI surface)
`inventory/handlers.py` subscribes to procurement/sales/manufacturing/quality events and auto-creates moves: goods receipts → RECEIPT moves (offset to GR/IR), sales deliveries → ISSUE moves (offset to COGS), sales returns → RECEIPT moves (offset reversing COGS), production component issues → ISSUE moves (offset to WIP), production finish → RECEIPT (offset reversing WIP), quality rejections → ADJUSTMENT-out (scrap) or TRANSFER (block to quarantine bin). None of these are separate endpoints — they'll simply appear as rows in `/stock-moves` with a `reference` field carrying the driving document's number (GR number, delivery number, etc.), and the docflow chain links them. Your move-ledger UI should treat `reference` as a display-only breadcrumb, not something the frontend creates for these cases (only manual RECEIPT/ISSUE/TRANSFER/ADJUSTMENT via the form hits the direct endpoint).

## 6. Async/background-job pattern

Only ONE inventory job: `COUNT_POST_JOB = "inventory.count_post"`, registered via `@register_job(COUNT_POST_JOB)` in `service/count_jobs.py`. Threshold constant `COUNT_POST_SYNC_MAX_VARIANCES = 200` (mirrors finance's depreciation-run=100 / bank-import=1000 precedent). The router (`count_router.post_stock_count`) estimates variance count from the snapshot (`count_variance_estimate`), and if it exceeds 200, submits the job and returns `202 JobSubmitted`; otherwise posts inline and returns `200 StockCountRead`. Job handler just delegates to the same `post_count` service function, returning `{count_id, count_number, status, adjustment_move_count}` as its job result payload — poll via the generic `/api/v1/jobs/{job_id}` the same way finance's bank-import/depreciation-run UIs already do.

No other CSV-import-style background job exists in this module (no bulk item import, no bulk move import) — item/warehouse/bin CRUD is one-row-at-a-time only.

## 7. Service-layer business semantics summary

- **On-hand computation:** stored/maintained projection (`inv_stock_quants`), NOT a live sum — updated transactionally with every move, deleted at zero, `CHECK >= 0`.
- **Valuation method:** per-item, chosen at create (defaulted from category), either MOVING_AVERAGE (full-precision average recomputed on receipt, quantized-and-flushed-to-price-difference on final issue) or FIFO (layer-based, oldest-first consumption, exact reversal via replay).
- **Variance reconciliation:** posts as ordinary ADJUSTMENT stock moves through the standard costing/event-bus pipeline → finance posts the journal in the same transaction. No bespoke "count journal."
- **Reversibility:** moves reversible once via a dedicated `/reverse` endpoint (new opposite move, never an edit); counts are NOT reversible once POSTED (terminal) — corrections require a new count or a direct ADJUSTMENT move.
- **Over-issue protection:** `InsufficientStockError` (422) pre-flight, backed by a DB CHECK constraint.
